questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How bodybuilders train for big competitions
How to cook eggs for a healthy breakfast
Why supermarkets are selling less meat
The protein trend and whether we forget fibre
questions.why: They discuss the focus on protein and ask whether we're forgetting other nutrients like fibre.

questions.q: What is Neil's and Georgie's favourite kind of protein?
options: Chicken
Eggs
Fish
Beans
questions.why: Neil says an egg is his favourite protein, and Georgie was going to say that too.

questions.q: What does Ruth Alexander notice in supermarkets?
options: Lots of high-protein items, like lentil pasta
Fewer products that contain any protein
Much more sugar-free chocolate on the shelves
Mostly fresh fruit and vegetables at the front
questions.why: She sees high-protein products in abundance, like lentil and chickpea pasta and bean bread.

questions.q: According to Neil, how are some products made to look 'high-protein'?
options: They are made smaller and sold at higher prices
They are sold only in gyms and sports shops
They are repackaged, or have beans added
They are cooked for longer to change them
questions.why: He says items with protein are re-packaged as 'high-protein', and others have beans and pulses added.

questions.q: What does Scott Dicker say about how consumers see protein?
options: They think it's sometimes good and sometimes bad
They always see it as healthy, unlike carbs and fat
They think it's too expensive
They don't care about it
questions.why: He says carbs and fat are sometimes good, sometimes bad, but protein has a 'continuous health halo'.

questions.q: What does Neil suggest about adding protein powder to foods?
options: It can make unhealthy food seem healthy
It always makes food healthier
It makes food taste much better
It is banned in some countries
questions.why: He says food once considered unhealthy is now called healthy just because protein powder is added.

questions.q: What does Dr Karan Rajan say about people's interest in fibre?
options: People have always paid enough attention to it
Nobody is really interested in fibre at all
Fibre is much less important than protein
People ignored it, but interest is growing
questions.why: He says historically probably not, but 'the tide is turning' and more people are interested.

questions.q: Which tip does Dr Karan give for getting more fibre?
options: Drinking protein shakes after exercise
Eating more eggs and meat every day
Adding seeds or nuts to snacks and meals
Eating only fruit for breakfast
questions.why: He mentions tips like adding certain seeds or nuts to snacks.
